goal: Fix the live archival defect in `teardownCmd` (`scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs`): the `task` argument to `shouldArchive` is currently the hardcoded literal `{ outcome: 'ok' }`, so a run whose every dispatch completed ok but whose overall work the orchestrator refused by hand has its task dir and state dir DELETED rather than archived — the audit trail is destroyed exactly when it matters most. Add an enum-closed `--outcome <ok|refused>` flag to the `teardown` verb, defaulting to `ok` so today's behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte for every existing caller, and pass `{ outcome: <resolved flag> }` to `shouldArchive` in place of the literal. Add two new exported frozen constants (`TEARDOWN_OUTCOMES`, `DEFAULT_TEARDOWN_OUTCOME`), validate the flag BEFORE any side effect so an out-of-enum value refuses with exit 2 having closed no surface and deleted nothing, mention the flag on the teardown-order line of `references/cmux-dispatch.md`, and pin all of it with tests.
constraints: conventions.md "Prefer structural impossibility to a test assertion, and a whitelist to a blacklist" (2026-08-01) — `--outcome` is a CLOSED whitelist enum held in a frozen exported array; an unrecognised value REFUSES, is never coerced, never defaulted-on-typo, and the drift-guard test is only a meta-check that the constraint hasn't been widened.

conventions.md "`execution_mode` canonical values ... Enforced by frozen exports in `scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs` (`EXECUTION_MODES`, ...) + a deepEqual drift guard" (2026-08-03) — mirror that exact shape: `Object.freeze([...])`, exported, plus a `assert.deepEqual` drift-guard test. Quote the RAW supplied spelling in the refusal message (`JSON.stringify(args.outcome)`), exactly as `readExecutionMode` and `phaseCmd` do.

conventions.md "'Never logs the secret' and 'exactly-once side effect' acceptance criteria are vacuous unless proven by mutation" (2026-08-02) — the load-bearing negative test here is behavioural: reverting the call site to the hardcoded `{ outcome: 'ok' }` MUST turn the suite red. Verify this by actually performing the revert locally, confirming red, then restoring.

conventions.md "A newly-added prose safety rule in a doctrine file ... needs its own test pin the same round" (2026-08-08) — the `references/cmux-dispatch.md` teardown-order edit gets its pin in `test/cmux-dispatch-doc.test.mjs` in this same commit.

conventions.md "A doc-prose test file's header 'owned elsewhere' registry ..." / per-section single-owner (2026-08-08) — `test/cmux-dispatch-doc.test.mjs` is the ONLY owner of `references/cmux-dispatch.md` prose assertions. Put the doc pin there, never in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

If you must reference the old shape in a comment, phrase it so the guard's regex cannot match (e.g. "a hardcoded ok literal").

conventions.md "Every functional commit bumps the `version` field in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and the commit message ends with `; bump 0.<major>.<minor>`" (2026-08-01) — bump 0.1.71 → 0.1.72. Suggested commit message (from the design record): `feat: dispatch — teardown --outcome gates archival on the caller's verdict, not a hardcoded ok; bump 0.1.72`.

conventions.md 2026-08-08 "Verify a dispatched coder's commit actually landed" — run `git log --oneline -1` and `git status` yourself after committing and report the real SHA in your return. A `status: done` with uncommitted work has happened twice in this repo.

`scripts/cmux/contract.mjs` is a CONTRACT-FREEZE file and must NOT be touched. `shouldArchive`'s own signature and fail-closed logic are unchanged by this slice — the fix is entirely on the caller side.
No lint/typecheck tooling exists in this repo (plain JS + `node --test`), so the tests ARE the enforcement mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: `node dispatch.mjs teardown --task <slug> --outcome refused` archives BOTH the task dir and the state dir even when every dispatch record's outcome is `ok` — asserted as `res.json.task_dir.archived === true`, `res.json.state_dir.archived === true`, both archive paths exist on disk, and `existsSync(ctx.paths.taskDir) === false` / `existsSync(ctx.paths.stateDir) === false`. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

`--outcome ok` with all-ok dispatch records DELETES exactly as today: `task_dir.deleted === true`, `task_dir.archived === false`, and the same for `state_dir`. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

NO flag supplied ⇒ byte-for-byte identical to today's behaviour — the regression guard. The four pre-existing teardown tests at `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs (line 2286)`, `:2300`, `:2987`, `:3000` (all of which call `teardownCmd({}, ctx)`) must pass UNMODIFIED, and one new test asserts `teardownCmd({}, ctx)` and `teardownCmd({ outcome: 'ok' }, ctx)` produce the same archived/deleted booleans on equivalent fixtures. Covered by `node --test test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

An unrecognised `--outcome` value refuses as a `UsageError` (which `main()` maps to exit code 2 at `dispatch.mjs:2747-2750`), validated BEFORE any side effect: zero cmux invocations (log length unchanged, mirroring the assertion at `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs (lines 2208-2214)`) AND `existsSync(ctx.paths.taskDir) === true` / `existsSync(ctx.paths.stateDir) === true` after the throw — nothing closed, nothing deleted, nothing archived. Test at least `'bogus'`, `'OK'` (wrong case), `''` (empty string) and `'refused '` (trailing space) all refusing; the refusal message names the allowed set from the exported constant and quotes the raw supplied spelling. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

Drift guard: `assert.deepEqual(TEARDOWN_OUTCOMES, ['ok', 'refused'])` and `assert.equal(DEFAULT_TEARDOWN_OUTCOME, 'ok')`, mirroring the `EXECUTION_MODES` guard at `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs (lines 254-256)`. Widening the enum or changing the default then requires a deliberate test edit. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

Source-text guard: reading `scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs`, the hardcoded-literal call shape (regex tolerant of whitespace, e.g. /shouldArchive\(\s*\{\s*outcome:\s*'ok'\s*\}/) does NOT appear anywhere in the file, AND the `teardownCmd` body does contain a `shouldArchive({ outcome: ... })` call fed by the resolved flag. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

`--keep-artifacts` still forces archival regardless of `--outcome` — assert `archived === true` for BOTH `{ 'keep-artifacts': true, outcome: 'ok' }` and `{ 'keep-artifacts': true, outcome: 'refused' }` on an all-ok fixture. Extends the existing test at `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs (line 2317)`. Covered by a new test in `test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs`.

MUTATION-PROVEN NEGATIVE (the acceptance criterion the issue states verbatim): reverting the call site to the hardcoded `{ outcome: 'ok' }` fails the suite. The coder must actually perform this revert locally, observe at least the `--outcome refused` test go RED, restore the fix, and report the observed failing test name(s) in the `validation` field of the return. A green suite alone does not satisfy this criterion.
